mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to increased near-term discounting of equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of FEDFUNDS rising periods, or IC > 0.05 over 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.0%, labor market slack increases, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative in >50% of UNRATE < 3.0% events, or IC < -0.1 over 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in GDPC1 (real GDP) followed by a decline in HOUST (inflation) predicts positive 20-day SPX returns as growth outpaces inflation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth quarter-on-quarter > 3% and HOUST < previous quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >40% of such events, or IC < 0.05 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 100 suggests supply-side weakness, leading to negative 5-day SPX forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are non-negative in >60% of INDPRO < 100 periods, or IC > 0.2 over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative due to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of such episodes, or IC > 0.1 over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) above 150,000 suggests labor market strength, producing positive 60-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in >40% of such events, or IC < -0.05 over 1 year.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS > 700 billion and a decline in CPIAUCSL below 305 indicate strong demand with cooling prices, predicting positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >50% of such events, or IC < 0.1 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of UNRATE above 4% signals tight labor markets, raising wage growth and reducing real equity valuations, resulting in negative 5-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive in >70% of UNRATE > 4% periods, or IC > 0.15 over 3 months.
